Risk Factors and Limitations: The compliance gate may fail (the reader keeps its prior over a named appliance); then the swap is implausible to this reader and the study stops rather than strengthening the wrapper. Name swaps are a stylised binding: the claim is about the existence of a cheap non-committing probe, a property of real environments (silent API or UI failures), not about renaming. The untestable regime bundles undetectability with irreversibility because an undetectable-but-reversible failure is probe-able by redundancy (a 30-token 'do the step at both appliances' rule needs no binding); that third regime is a stated limit of the contrast and is not run. Contents of the swapped receptacles are not rewritten (a fridge full of plates is a weak leak); the construction check on D(S0, untestable) bounds it. Table routing depends on the receptacle-count signature identifying the floorplan (checked mechanically; colliding kitchens with the same binding are merged, with different bindings excluded); the ~30-row table is this benchmark's natural size and routing over hundreds of rows is not tested. Only Qwen3-32B; the reader's ability to execute a run-time probe or route a table may differ by backbone. W+/W- contexts are per game and uncached across games, the most expensive cells. The 200 held-out train games may differ in difficulty from valid_seen (stratum analysis). Same-kitchen hit rate below .8 would force a stronger key before any confirmatory cell.
Addresses gap: G2 (retriever vs fixed/static artifact never isolated): the residual of scene-keyed retrieval over the best static arm (static3 and its compiled augmentations from the same bank) is measured under a planted binding with the feedback regime manipulated on the same games, and the binding-created part is separated from the natural +17.2 by the within-game swap penalty; G3 (no whole-bank arm): the whole bank is run with the binding's presence randomised within game; cross-axis G6/G10 (retrieval vs knowledge never separated; relatedness threshold unmeasured) are attacked by making the binding's testability, not its presence, the manipulated variable, and by the oracle-key and oracle-name arms that bound what any lookup can add.
Not a restatement of: Prior-result bullet 'unseen ~ seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure, not the scene': this idea plants scene bindings and predicts that the retrieval residual over the best static arm is the natural +17.2 plus a binding-created term that exists only when the environment gives no probe and only against a static artifact that names a test instead of enumerating; a 60-token rule removes the term under the testable regime and an observation-keyed table removes it under the untestable one. Digest card arxiv:2605.22219 (SGR-Bench: failures come from the wrong site-specific state; whether stored procedures or prior trajectories would fix it is untested): this idea builds the stored procedures (table and rule) and the trajectory retrieval, and claims that which of them is needed is decided by whether the wrong state is detectable before committing, a property it manipulates on the same games rather than names.
Changes made: P1: the stale-playbook loss under untestable is now a construction check (reported, not scored); the gate is S3 (per-game oracle names) vs S0, which measures compliance and can fail. P2: kept open; restated as swap penalties, TOST margin set above the +-8 half-width, type-agnostic clause (T0) added, and the self-recovery outcome named as a result rather than a design failure. P3 (headline): estimand changed to D(R3, untestable) with S1's inertness stated as construction; the retriever is estimated separately by a pre-registered same-kitchen hit rate and the R3o oracle-key arm, so a null is attributable; stated why P3 is not implied by P1. P4: margin above the half-width by doubling the swapped cell (complementary assignments, 528 pairs, floor +-8); permuted-table placebo cut as forced; raw R3 - S2 stated against the measured +17.2 natural residual and the manipulation that keeps the binding from adding to it named (enumeration); T1 clause added. P5 (seen-unseen gap) removed and all unseen cells cut; 'Not a restatement of' rewritten around the regime x artifact interaction. P6 (whole bank): W+/W- with the same-kitchen item's presence randomised within game, paired, sizes and floor stated. P7 -> P5 (cost): threshold moved above the mechanical step count; an upper bound (post-probe flailing) and an unswapped over-testing clause added so the estimand can come out against the hypothesis. Design: untestable regime made one-shot (silent commit) because an undetectable-but-reversible failure is probe-able by redundancy and would let a 30-token rule bypass the binding; baseline changed to static3 (best measured) with type-agnostic playbook arms retained as controls; goal-keyed k3 and k0 at q = .5 cut; arithmetic 17,036 episodes, ~11.5 h on two A100s plus one day of engineering. Short Hypothesis: the contradiction between 'residual over the best compiled artifact' and 'the table matches the query' resolved: the residual over the best static arm is the natural residual once the artifact enumerates the binding; the binding-created term appears only against a non-enumerating artifact under the untestable regime. The central claim was not softened: it still predicts a regime x artifact interaction with both halves scored on the same games, and the one-shot regime makes the risky half harder to pass, not easier.

Name: compile_the_statistics_not_the_trajectory
Title: What Retrieval Cannot Carry: Cross-Episode Location Statistics Compiled From the Bank Beat Retrieved Trajectories on Search-Bound Tasks
Short Hypothesis: A compiled artifact can hold a cross-episode aggregate (object -> receptacle location frequencies) that no set of k retrieved trajectories contains. On ALFWorld's search-bound types (pick-and-place, pick-two, look-at-in-light) a ~300-token, type-agnostic, cached cheatsheet compiled by rule from the expert pool recovers at least the Gate-0 retrieval gain on those types (~+10) over no memory at zero uncached prefill. Its value comes from aggregation, not coverage or scaffold: a coverage-matched table built from one sampled trajectory per object class loses most of it, a row-deranged table loses all of it, and the raw 80-item bank in context does not reproduce it unless the table compiled from those same items is added explicitly. Added to the best static arm (Measurement C's static3), the statistic removes the residual that k=3 retrieval keeps over it on the search-bound types (C: ~+9 there); it is not expected to touch the procedure-bound residual (+20..+27), which is reported as the scope boundary, not claimed.
Related Work: Measurement A on this node shows the retrieval gain is procedure-bound (unseen ~ seen) and smaller on the pick types (+15/+18/-5) than on heat/cool/clean (+39..+55). Measurement C (2026-09-09) finds the best static arm is static3 (3 fixed type-conditioned exemplars, ~430 tokens): static3 - k0 = +12.4, k3 - static3 = +17.2 with the residual concentrated on clean/heat/cool (+20..+27) and only +10..+12 on pick types, +4.8 on look-at (CI including 0); the type-agnostic six-procedure prompt is +9.5 over k0 and -20.1 under k3. No static arm in A or C carries anything a single trajectory cannot. Strategy graphs (2511.07800), verifier-promoted skill graphs (2512.23760), tutorials (2606.03951) and ICAL insight exemplars (2406.14596) compile trajectories but never at matched tokens against raw retrieval and never separate distillation from aggregation (G1); SkillEvolBench (2605.24117) finds raw reuse often beats distilled skills but its skills are procedures, not statistics. Dynamic Cheatsheet (2504.07952) accumulates insights at test time but never compares against retrieval of the raw episodes or varies the amount of experience compiled. An LLM-free ALFWorld agent (WCCIS 2026, 'Zero-Shot Embodied Decision Making with Structured Prior Knowledge') hand-builds object-location priors and shows they matter for a symbolic controller, but does not compile them from experience, vary aggregation depth, or compare with an LLM reader's retrieval. Object-search work in robotics (2607.00022 PerSim; 2603.05642 SymSearch) uses population-frequency placement priors, confirming the mechanism exists outside the agent-memory literature. Archived: compile_dont_retrieve (6.0) observed the read to be inert; here the compiled artifact is given content retrieval cannot have and that content is manipulated (depth at fixed coverage, derangement, no-experience prior). optimizer_substitutes_for_memory_scaffold (5.22) could not separate scaffold from content; the deranged-table placebo separates them by construction of the arm, not of the outcome.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers compare retrieval with no memory; the cheapest alternative, a fixed prompt compiled once from the same experience, is rarely run, and when compiled artifacts are studied their gain is not attributed. We isolate one thing compilation can do that per-query retrieval structurally cannot: aggregate across episodes. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B and the 1,465-item expert pool on this node, we compile by rule a ~300-token cheatsheet of object -> receptacle location frequencies (from the 'take X from Y' step of each trajectory) and place it, type-agnostically, in the instruction slot as a cached static prefix. On the 134 search-bound games (pick-and-place, pick-two, look-at-in-light) at 8 seeds we compare it, within one serving session, with no memory, k=3 retrieval, Measurement C's best static arm (static3), a depth ladder that varies how many trajectories per object class are aggregated at fixed coverage (1, 4, all), a token-matched deranged table, a same-format table written by Qwen3-32B without the bank, the raw 80-item bank in context (11k tokens, cached) with and without the table compiled from those same 80 items, and static3 plus the cheatsheet. Task success is primary; receptacles visited before the target is taken is the process measure; uncached prefill per episode is logged under vLLM prefix caching. The claim: on search-bound types the compiled statistic recovers at least the Gate-0 retrieval gain (~+10) over no memory at zero uncached prefill; most of that value disappears when each row is a single sample and all of it when rows are deranged; the long-context reader does not compute the statistic from the raw items; and added to the best static arm the statistic removes the ~+9 residual that k=3 retains over it on these types, while the +20..+27 procedure-bound residual is outside its scope and reported as such.
Experiments: Bank: expert pool (1,465 trajectories). Compiler (rule, no LLM): from each trajectory take the receptacle of the first successful 'take <obj> from <recep>' action; per object class (~30) emit the top-3 receptacle classes with count and percentage; ~300 tokens; identical for every game and type; placed in the instruction slot as a cached static prefix. Aggregation-depth ladder at fixed coverage (replaces the n-trajectory ladder, whose low rungs confounded coverage with depth): cheatsheet_d samples, for every object class c, min(d, n_c) trajectories containing that class and compiles the row from them; d = 1 (one sample per class, every class covered, ~150 tokens, three uniform draws), d = 4 (one draw, exploratory), d = all (the full table). Placebos: shuffled_all (receptacle lists deranged across object classes, identical tokens and format); LLM-prior (Qwen3-32B fills the same format for the same object classes and receptacle vocabulary from its own knowledge, no bank, generated once, token-matched). Whole bank: 80 expert items (~140 tokens each, ~11k tokens, cached) selected by a stated rule - stratified by task type and, within type, to cover every object class at least twice; fixed order per seed; whole-bank_80 + cheatsheet_80 adds the table compiled from exactly those 80 items (~250 tokens). Cells: cell S = the 134 search-bound games (pick-and-place, pick-two, look-at-in-light; 59 unseen + 75 seen) x 8 seeds = 1,072 paired (game, seed) cells per arm; seeds 1-2 coincide with Measurement C's cells. Confirmatory arms on cell S (12, all run fresh in one serving session so every contrast is paired within-session): k0; k3 retrieval (~430 uncached tokens); static3 (C's best static arm, 3 fixed type-conditioned exemplars, ~430 tokens cached); cheatsheet_all; shuffled_all; LLM-prior; cheatsheet_d1 x 3 draws; static3 + cheatsheet_all (~730 tokens cached); whole-bank_80; whole-bank_80 + cheatsheet_80. Name: retrieval_timing_is_budgeting
Title: When to Retrieve Is Only a Budget Question: A Harm-Mass Bound on the Value of Retrieval Timing for Experience Memory, Tested at Two Distractor Levels, With Failure-Keyed Retrieval at Stall Against Planted Recoveries, Coverage-Matched Self Detours and a Compiled Rulebook
Short Hypothesis: With retrieved content, cached prefix and message format held fixed, the value of any retrieval-timing policy (start, fixed schedule, on stall, learned) over always-retrieve is bounded above by the harm mass: the fraction of episodes on which retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt solves, beyond test-retest flips. On ALFWorld we measure the harm mass as a paired-table estimand at two distractor levels of one expert bank and predict it is inside the +/-8 floor at the natural bank and above it with mislabelled twins; stall-triggered retrieval then sits within +/-8 of always-retrieve at the natural bank in both directions and, at the twin bank, gains over always-retrieve by at least 8 net but never more than the harm mass plus the floor, so timing re-trades uncached tokens for the same success and cannot buy more. A failure-keyed query at stall beats a content-free key only when the bank holds matching recoveries: at matched coverage the agent's own curated detours do as well as planted recoveries, the natural self pool does not, and a compiled recovery rulebook in the cached prefix matches planted retrieval at zero uncached cost.
Related Work: arXiv:2607.24010 (When Should Active RAG Retrieve?) recasts active retrieval as marginal correctness over the no-retrieval answer under a budget, but on QA with document retrieval, without a harm-mass estimand on paired seeds, a stall trigger or caching costs. ProactAgent (arXiv:2604.20572, 'Ask Only When Needed') retrieves proactively from memory and skills for lifelong agents without an always-retrieve-at-matched-content arm or an upper bound on the decision. FLARE (arXiv:2305.06983) and Adaptive-RAG (arXiv:2403.14403) trigger retrieval by uncertainty or complexity in QA. Reflexion (arXiv:2303.11366) conditions on failure across trials, not within-episode stalls, and has no static control. Digest: arXiv:2607.07380 (hidden-state uncertainty decides when to retrieve; no always/never baselines), s2:93def179dbebdaf187c0bce1f494a2bbd39ddc19 (RL proxy decides when/how; cost unaccounted), arXiv:2510.16724 (survey; no common protocol), arXiv:2607.20972 (cue-triggered deterministic injection beats voluntary reads; no harm bound or compiled control), arXiv:2505.00234 (self-generated examples for sequential decision tasks, the on-policy bank). Archived ideas do not address timing; compile_dont_retrieve concerns the goal-conditioned read at episode start.
Abstract: Adaptive retrieval papers ask when to retrieve but do not report what a perfect answer to that question would be worth. For experience memory under prompt caching the accounting is simple: with the retrieved content, the cached prefix and the message format held fixed, a timing policy can add success over always-retrieve only on episodes where retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt would have solved. We call that fraction the harm mass and measure it as a pre-registered paired-table estimand on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds, static3 cached prefix from Measurement C, one k=3 goal-keyed block appended at step 0 or later): P(static succeeds and retrieval fails) minus the same discordance between two static runs, at two distractor levels of one expert bank (natural, and a 1:1 mislabelled-twin bank in which goal-keyed retrieval returns a wrong-type trajectory in about half the slots). Predictions: the harm mass is inside the +/-8 floor at the natural bank and above it with twins; stall-triggered retrieval (two consecutive 'Nothing happens' or a repeated action) is within +/-8 of always-retrieve at the natural bank in both directions; at the twin bank it gains over always-retrieve by at least 8 net and by no more than the harm mass plus the floor, and a fixed step-10 schedule does the same as the trigger. We then ask whether the query at stall matters, separating key from content in a k=1 2x2 (failure key vs random key; planted-recovery bank vs expert pool) and manipulating recovery coverage in the agent's own detour pool (natural coverage measured by a validated tagger; curated recovery windows at coverage near 1). Predictions: the failure key beats a random key only with planted recoveries; curated self detours match planted recoveries at matched coverage while the natural pool falls short; and a ~200-token recovery rulebook in the cached prefix matches planted retrieval at zero uncached cost. The output is an accuracy-cost frontier on which the timing decision moves along the frontier rather than above it, with the bound tested as an inequality at a level where it binds and a test of whether any query is more than decorative at stall time.
Experiments: Setting as in Measurement A/C: ALFWorld 274 games x 2 seeds, identical seeds across arms, Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas with prefix caching. Shared prefix: static3 (3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, ~430 tokens, cached), the best static arm from Measurement C; every arm sits on it. Retrieval block: k=3 goal-keyed items (~430 tokens) appended as one environment-style message with identical text and format whether appended at step 0 (always), at step 10 (schedule) or at the stall (stall arms), so content, prefix and format are fixed across timing arms and only the delivery step varies. Banks: natural expert bank; distractor bank = the expert bank plus one mislabelled twin per item (the item's goal sentence attached to the trajectory of a different-type expert item that shares the target object), so goal-keyed retrieval ties twins with originals and returns a wrong-type trajectory in about half the k=3 slots (Measurement C's wrong-type placebo blind1 is -3 under k0, about -15 under static3, the reason to expect harm); planted-recovery bank (five ALFWorld failure modes: closed receptacle, wrong receptacle, object already held, wrong object instance, missing 'go to'; one ~40-token recovery item each, keyed by failure text; coverage 1.0 by construction); self pool = 1,892 self-generated successes with detours, indexed by failed-action windows (natural level), and its curated subset of windows the tagger marks as a failure mode followed by a recovery within three steps (curated level). Coverage c(pool) = fraction of stall-firing episodes (from cell 4's firing log) whose tagged failure mode has at least one same-mode recovery window in the pool; the rule-based tagger reads the last three actions and observations and is validated on 100 hand-labelled stall windows (agreement >= 0.8 required before the self-pool cells run). Where the expert bank exceeds the ~80-item whole-context limit, the truncated whole-bank arm is Measurement C's k-sweep (k7 = +19.5 over static3) and the start read is held fixed at k=3 here. Stall trigger: first occurrence of two consecutive 'Nothing happens' or a repeated (observation, action) pair; threshold 2 confirmatory, threshold 5 optional. Queries at stall: goal sentence (k=3, matching always); failure key = last three actions and observations (k=1); random key = uniform draw from the pool (k=1); k=1 for all failure-key and random-key cells because the planted bank holds one item per mode. Estimand for P1 on the 548 (game, seed) rows: D(L) = P(static3_A succeeds and always(L) fails), D0 = P(static3_A succeeds and static3_B fails), Delta_harm(L) = D(L) - D0, with static3_A the Measurement C cell and static3_B a fresh re-run; cluster-bootstrap CI over games. The cross-fitted oracle (decide on static3_A, score static3_B where it succeeded and always elsewhere) is computed from the same cells and reported as a descriptive upper bound; no oracle cell is run. Cells (548 episodes each, ~30 min per cell with both replicas busy): (1) static3_B re-run; (2) always-natural; (3) always-distractor; (4) stall goal-key k=3 threshold 2, natural; (5) stall goal-key k=3 threshold 2, distractor; (6) step-10 schedule goal-key k=3, natural; (7) stall failure-key k=1, expert pool; (8) stall failure-key k=1, planted; (9) stall random-key k=1, planted; (10) stall failure-key k=1, self natural; (11) stall failure-key k=1, self curated; (12) static3 + recovery rulebook (the five planted items concatenated, ~200 tokens, cached; the whole-bank arm of the planted bank); (13) rulebook + stall failure-key k=1 planted. Optional if time remains: (14) curated-self whole-bank arm, cached, truncated to the top-N recovery windows by tag confidence, type-balanced, that fit 16k with the longest trajectory (the brief's whole-bank rule; exploratory); (15) stall goal-key threshold 5, natural. Arithmetic: 13 confirmatory cells x 548 = 7,124 episodes, ~3.25 h wall on two A100s; with both optional cells 8,220 episodes, ~3.75 h; inside the original 4 h envelope. Logging per episode and arm: success, steps, firing step, uncached prefill tokens (prompt tokens minus cached tokens from vLLM), cache hit rate; accuracy vs uncached tokens per episode is the cost axis. Pre-registered order: cells 1-3 (P1 decides whether the distractor level exists), then 4-6 (P2, P6), then 8, 9, 7 (P3), then 10-11 (P4), then 12-13 (P5), then the optional cells.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: never-retrieve = static3 (cached; the best static arm from Measurement C, +12.4 over k0); always-retrieve = static3 plus the same k=3 goal-keyed block appended at step 0 (uncached block, ~430 tokens per episode; its residual over static3_B is checked against Measurement C's +17.2 +/- 5); fixed step-10 schedule (timing without a trigger); random-key-at-stall on the planted bank (content-free key, pool fixed); failure-key-at-stall on the expert pool (key fixed, no recovery content); compiled recovery rulebook in the cached prefix (the static counterpart of planted retrieval and the whole-bank arm of the 5-item planted bank); curated-self whole-bank arm (cached, truncated; optional); cross-fitted oracle computed from static3_A, static3_B and always (descriptive upper bound, no cell). Type conditioning: every arm shares the static3 prefix, so type conditioning is constant in every contrast; the rulebook and planted items are keyed by failure mode, not task type; Measurement C's instr_all (type-agnostic, -20.1 under k3) and blind1 (wrong type) are the standing references. Manipulated properties, two levels each on one environment: distractor rate of the expert bank (natural vs 1:1 mislabelled twins) for the harm mass; recovery coverage of the self pool (natural c_nat vs curated c_cur, both measured) for the failure key. Ablations: rulebook with vs without stall retrieval on top (P5); stall threshold 2 vs 5 (optional); step-10 schedule vs stall trigger (P2 secondary).
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline; harm mass small at the natural bank, large with distractors): Estimand Delta_harm(L) = P(static3_A succeeds and always(L) fails) - P(static3_A succeeds and static3_B fails) on the same 548 rows, cluster-bootstrap CI over games. Prediction: Delta_harm(natural) < 8 points and Delta_harm(distractor) >= 8 points. Falsified if Delta_harm(natural) >= 8 (retrieval from the natural expert bank breaks more than 8 percent of static-solved episodes beyond test-retest, so timing policies have headroom at the natural bank and the 'inside the floor' clause is wrong; producible: Measurement C's look-at type is +4.8 with CI including 0 and pick types +10 to +12, so a harm mass of 8 to 12 points concentrated on pick and look-at episodes is reachable) or if Delta_harm(distractor) < 8 (the reader ignores mislabelled twins, the high level failed as a manipulation, P6 is not run). Title: Confusable, Not Long: The Whole-Bank-in-Context Route Loses to Top-k Retrieval Only as Near-Miss Trajectories Accumulate
Short Hypothesis: On a six-procedure trajectory bank read by Qwen3-32B, the whole bank as a cached static prefix matches goal-sentence top-3 retrieval on task success up to the 16k context no matter how many redundant or off-domain items are added, and falls behind only as the count of near-miss items (same object and receptacle words, different procedure) grows. Retrieval is hurt by near-miss items too, but its exposure is capped at k items whose cross-type share equals the bank's share, so at fixed share it is flat in count. At matched length, composition therefore costs the whole-bank route more than retrieval; this route x composition interaction replicates on an independent bank draw and is larger for the weaker reader (Qwen3-8B) on the same size grid, so the bank size at which the routes cross is set by composition and reader, not prompt length.
Related Work: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank (arxiv:2608.22695) shows in-context routing over a capability registry collapsing as the registry grows while retrieve-then-rank degrades gracefully, but scores Match@1 with one router model and grows the number of distinct options, not the number of confusable copies. Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) and arxiv:2412.16926 find that long-context ICL gains come from attention to the similar examples and that selection matters less as shots grow, on classification tasks; MANYICLBENCH (arxiv:2411.07130) separates similar-sample from all-sample learning; arxiv:2510.16809 finds a few well-chosen examples beating many on code translation. arxiv:2607.26497 measures a corpus-size crossover between agentic search and BM25 on documents with one reader; arxiv:2603.04814 measures Mem0 against long context on conversational QA with one model; arxiv:2411.05000 shows effective context shorter than advertised on synthetic threads. The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) shows agents adopting conflicting retrieved memory; SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) reports clutter from larger libraries under an unspecified selection. None of these grows a trajectory bank while holding the procedure count fixed and separating redundant count, off-domain length and confusable count, scores task success, and checks whether the crossover moves with the reader.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers assume a bank of trajectories must be queried because the whole bank will not fit or will not be read well, and the long-context literature reports crossovers between retrieval and in-context reading measured on documents with one reader. We ask what property of a trajectory bank actually makes the whole-bank-in-context route fall behind top-k retrieval on task success. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we grow a six-item seed bank (one expert exemplar per task type) to 12-80 items in three ways that hold the six procedures fixed: redundant growth (same-type items whose object-receptacle combos collide with no other type), off-domain filler (token-matched trajectories from another text game), and near-miss growth (every added item has a twin of another type with the same object and receptacle, so half the bank is confusable). Each bank is read whole as a cached static prefix or through goal-sentence top-3 retrieval, on the same 274 games and two seeds, with the Measurement C static arms as the baseline, a type-conditioned retrieval arm and logged top-3 composition to show that retrieved twins are actually adopted rather than merely present, a fixed uniformly random 80-item subset as the selection control, and an independent second bank draw on which the route x composition interaction is confirmed. We predict the whole-bank route is flat under redundant and filler growth and declines with the near-miss count, while retrieval is hurt by twins but flat in count at fixed share, so at matched length composition costs the whole-bank route more than retrieval, and more so for Qwen3-8B on the same size grid. Prefill tokens and GPU-seconds under prefix caching are logged for accuracy-cost curves.
Experiments:
- Bank construction from the expert pool (1,465 items). Seed S6 = one expert exemplar per task type, fixed. Growth rules that keep six procedures: R (redundant, near-miss share 0; sizes 12/48/80): add same-type items whose (object, receptacle) combo appears in no item of another type in the bank. N (near-miss, share 0.5; sizes 12/24/48/80): add items in cross-type twin pairs (same object and receptacle, different procedure; twins chosen so their first actions coincide), so at every size half the items have a twin in the bank; combos sampled from the pool's combo distribution. F (filler, size 80): S6 plus token-matched trajectories from public TextWorld cooking games in the same format with no ALFWorld nouns. U: one uniformly random fixed 80-subset of the pool (natural near-miss share measured and reported) as the G17 fixed-random-selection control. Replicate draw: a second N'-80 and R'-80 built by the same rules from disjoint items and disjoint twin combos with a fresh type-interleaved order. Per bank and size the coverage fraction (share of the 274 test goals whose combo has a twin pair in the bank) is logged. Item order type-interleaved, fixed per arm.
- Routes. WB: whole bank as a type-agnostic static prefix (vLLM prefix caching on, cache hit ratio logged). RET: goal-sentence top-3 from the same bank per episode (uncached), same retriever as Measurement A; per episode the top-3 type composition is logged (cross-type-in-top-3 rate = any item of another type in the top-3; strict twin rate = an item with the goal's object and receptacle and another type). RET-T: top-3 restricted to items of the goal's template type (type-conditioned by construction, reported under the type-conditioning rule), on N-48 only. - Near-miss harm may be small for a 32B reader because the goal sentence disambiguates the type (blind1 costs only 3 net against k0); that is the falsifying outcome of P2 and P3, not a design risk, and is reported as such.
- N and R banks contain different expert items because N items are selected for having twins; RET-T and the replicate draw bound this for retrieval and across draws, but no whole-bank analogue with twins' types relabelled exists, so a WB-only identity effect would appear as P2 confirmed with P4 falsified.
- Twin coverage of the 274 test goals grows with the number of pairs, so on the N ladder a count effect and a coverage effect are entangled; the covered/uncovered split and the logged coverage fraction separate them descriptively, not by manipulation.
- Only six procedures exist on ALFWorld, so the registry-growth regime of 2608.22695 (hundreds of distinct options) is not reachable here; the claim is limited to fixed-procedure banks, with WebShop as the stated extension.
- Twins are scarce for look-at-in-light and pick-two, so the N ladder's twin-bearing types are clean, heat, cool and pick-and-place; per-type results outside these are exploratory.
- 16k context caps the ladder at 80 items; a 32k extension on this node would cut concurrency and is not proposed.
- Whole-bank arms at 48/80 items run 2-3x slower per episode; the budget accounts for this and throughput is reported per arm.
- Qwen3-8B may be near its k=0 floor on ALFWorld; the precondition and the Qwen3-14B fallback keep P5 decidable, at the cost that the reader gap may be smaller than planned.
